relations.subject: service:eventing-service
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; object is a literal per the predicate's documented shape
relations.evidence: The memory quota for the Eventing Service must be a minimum of 256 MB. Couchbase does not support memory quota values smaller than 256 MB.

relations.subject: service:eventing-service
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; object is a literal
relations.evidence: Allow additional headroom on top of the 256 MB default for production workloads.

relations.subject: server:service-memory-quota
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate captures 'the subject's value is computed by uniform division across every instance of the object', a genuinely new relation shape (a derived/computed value, not a boolean requirement or a default)
relations.evidence:
The Eventing Service divides its total memory quota uniformly across all workers in all deployed functions:

Per-Worker quota = Total memory quota ÷ Total number of workers

relations.subject: eventing:worker-queue
relations.evidence: Each worker maintains a bounded input queue that receives changes to documents from the [Database Change Protocol (DCP)](../learn/clusters-and-availability/intra-cluster-replication.md#database-change-protocol) stream.

relations.subject: eventing:eventing-producer-process
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, extended to a third case beyond the Query/Backup services it was originally recorded for
relations.evidence: These processes effectively have no hard upper bound on memory usage. Collectively, these processes can consume all available system memory.

relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, extended to a third case beyond the Query/Backup services it was originally recorded for

relations.subject: eventing:eventing-producer-process
relations.evidence: In a containerized environment, all the Eventing runtime processes, like the eventing-producer and eventing-consumer, run within containers governed by cgroups with explicit memory limits. In this case, memory enforcement occurs at the cgroup level and not at the overall host system level.

relations.subject: eventing:eventing-consumer-process
relations.evidence: In a containerized environment, all the Eventing runtime processes, like the eventing-producer and eventing-consumer, run within containers governed by cgroups with explicit memory limits. In this case, memory enforcement occurs at the cgroup level and not at the overall host system level.

relations.subject: eventing:per-worker-quota
relations.evidence: When memory usage approaches the per-worker quota limit, the JavaScript runtime may trigger garbage collection to reclaim memory.

notable_absence.finding: No Enterprise/Community edition badge and no RBAC role requirement appear anywhere on this page, even though setting the Eventing Service memory quota is a cluster-configuration action of exactly the kind eventing-rbac.md (this batch) ties to Full Admin/Eventing Full Admin elsewhere. The page treats memory-quota configuration as purely an operational/capacity-planning concern, never crossing into who is allowed to change it.

cross_component_finding: eventing:worker-queue's DCP dependency connects directly to eventing-rbac.md's Data DCP Reader role (this batch): the role gates 'starting a DCP stream' on a Listen To Location keyspace, and this page is the mechanical follow-through - the resulting mutation feed lands in exactly the bounded per-worker queue described here, whose overflow throttles that same DCP stream. Neither page cross-references the other, so this connection is only visible by reading both.
cross_product_finding: This page's existence with no filename-identical twin in cloud/eventing/ was flagged going into this round as presumptive evidence that 'Capella manages Eventing memory automatically.' Direct evidence contradicts that framing: cloud/eventing/eventing-faq.md - the Capella twin of a DIFFERENT page in this same batch - states in its own 'Cluster Behavior' section that a Capella user can and sometimes must manually raise Eventing's memory allocation: 'This is typically related to resources given to the Eventing service and can be solved by adding additional Memory Quota to Eventing in the Cluster Settings. By default Eventing allocates 256 MB, raising this value to 512 MB will typically solve this resource issue (this is one of the rare instances that you may need to raise the Memory Quota for Eventing).' That is the identical 256 MB default and the identical 'Cluster Settings' framing this Server page uses, appearing on a page that is otherwise about Capella. So either the 'automatic management' premise is wrong for at least some Capella cluster tiers, or cloud/eventing/eventing-faq.md is carrying stale, un-adapted Server-tree language that Capella's docs never updated for its actually-managed memory model - both are real possibilities and no page in either tree resolves which. This is exactly the kind of disagreement this round was designed to surface: the absence of a twin page is not, by itself, reliable evidence of a genuine product difference, because a related page in the SAME Capella tree contradicts the inferred reason for the absence.
evidence_provenance: cross-page: the memory-quota-configurability quote is not on server/current/eventing/eventing-memory-quota.md itself; it is on the Capella twin of a sibling page in this batch (eventing-faq.md), cited here because it directly bears on whether this page's own topic (Eventing memory quota configuration) is Server-only as assumed going into this round.
